title: RAW INCOMPLETE: literal word explanations cross-check quoted spelling against ordinary lexical use
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Seek a complete source passage that explicitly removes, adds or substitutes a stated letter in a quoted word and also uses that word outside quotation. A single shared spelling channel must satisfy both the literal string equation and the surrounding complete linguistic account. This is stronger than guessing a name from a picture or treating semantic synonymy as graphic identity; no target word or actual source passage is identified.

design.human_mechanism: A compiler writes an ordinary explanation of a word, retaining the quoted spelling rather than silently replacing it with its referent. The same small writing table serves quoted names, named letters and surrounding prose. The reader distinguishes mentioning a string from using that word in a statement.
design.complete_content_requirement: The source must itself state the exact operation and its operand/result; analyst-computed resemblance does not qualify. Preserve the full passage, including reasons, exceptions and surrounding ordinary use. The operation is content, not a newly proposed transformation of every Voynich word.
design.bounded_writer_requirement: Before target selection, specify one complete source-to-writing table and tokenization/quotation policy that covers all ordinary prose and quoted strings. This raw card has not supplied that table, a historical source, a target or an alphabet binding. No dedicated q marker, new glyph, hidden gloss channel or free per-word dictionary is assumed.
design.prediction: A candidate complete reading must make the textually stated source-letter operation true and preserve the same operand spelling at separately occurring ordinary-use positions. A competing coherent interpretation that keeps the narrative but violates the explicitly stated letter operation fails. Letter names and the operation wording must themselves be read through the same fixed channel.
design.smallest_adequate_future_step: Acquire one independently authored complete primary passage with literal word manipulation, not a loose etymological resemblance, and exhibit one semantic rival that the exact equation actually separates. Only then review target ownership and a complete writer; do not start a native substring census.
design.why_it_may_help_translation: Meaning constrains exact source spelling, while repeated spelling constrains a proposed meaning. Unlike an arbitrary plausible paragraph, the text makes a checkable assertion about its own lexical material.
known_limits: No evidence that the Voynich text contains this genre or construction.
A genuinely false historical etymology may still be copied; require an exact written letter claim, not modern etymological correctness.
Unknown source language, unit mapping and quotation conventions remain unbound.
One string equation can leave many source readings; require all surviving complete alternatives and independent transfer, not uniqueness by assertion.
Any future Voynich word meaning needs its exact existing word profile and claim-bearing prior evidence; this card assigns none.
design.prior_distinction: IDEA868/881 concern name motivation and different referents, not an explicit letter-operation equation. IDEA975 quotes literal names inside a minim teaching writer but supplies no source-internal statement about changing those names. IP039 restores an abbreviated string; here the source itself describes a lexical operation and must also render its ordinary explanation.1357dedicated prefix quotation carrier remains failed and is not adopted.
design.review: Read live route; bounded ideas searches for metalinguistic, etymology, spelling, letter names, anagram; duplicates and route-check; inspected IDEA868 card including881followup and retained975/1357scope. These are navigation and raw-level distinctions, not an exhaustive novelty or reopening decision. No experiment selected.
design.access: No native payload, source acquisition, image, actual word meaning or experiment.
